title: Check a list of web addresses and print each HTTP status code
summary: Read addresses from a text file, ask each web server for its answer, and print the status code next to each address. Codes starting with 2 mean the page works. ERR means there was no answer at all.

aliases.text: http status check list of links
код ответа http для списка ссылок

steps.explain: Save the script from the script section as ~/bin/check-urls.sh, then make it executable.
Write the address list, one per line. Lines that are empty or start with # are skipped. This example has one good address and one that does not exist.

placeholders.name: URLS_FILE
placeholders.description: Text file with one web address per line

steps.explain: Check every address. Each line shows the HTTP status code, a tab, and the address. Redirects are followed, so you see the final answer.

placeholders.name: URLS_FILE
placeholders.description: Text file with one web address per line

steps.explain: Show only the problems: every line whose code does not start with 2. ERR means no answer at all, for example a name that does not resolve or a refused connection.
steps.expect: Only the lines with codes such as 404, 500 or ERR; nothing when all addresses work.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Check the HTTP status of every URL listed in a text file (one per line).
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped.
# Usage: check-urls.sh URLS_FILE
file="${1:?usage: $0 URLS_FILE}"
[[ -r "$file" ]] || { echo "cannot read $file" >&2; exit 1; }
while IFS= read -r url || [[ -n "$url" ]]; do
  [[ -z "$url" || "$url" == \#* ]] && continue
  code=$(curl -sSL --max-redirs 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 10 "$url" 2>/dev/null) || code="ERR"
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$code" "$url"
done < "$file"

output_guide.meaning: No HTTP answer at all: name lookup, connection or timeout problem.
The server answered, but the page does not exist.
